section_title: Why does Paul begin looking toward Jerusalem and Rome?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 21 After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia. “After I have been there,” he said, “I must see Rome as well.” 22 He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed for a time in the province of Asia.

context_lines: After the events in Ephesus, Paul resolves in the Spirit to travel through Macedonia and Achaia to Jerusalem, then to see Rome. He sends Timothy and Erastus ahead to Macedonia while remaining for a time in Asia. These two verses turn our attention from the long work in Ephesus toward the next stage of the journey.

Paul’s later account in [Romans 15:22–29](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/15.htm) explains a journey to Jerusalem with help from Macedonia and Achaia for poor believers there, along with his desire to visit Rome. This gives a wider view of his concerns without supplying a complete timetable for every plan in Acts.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly read these plans as continuing mission and care for the churches, directed toward Jerusalem and beyond it. Paul makes practical arrangements and sends helpers; dependence on the Spirit is not presented as the absence of planning or shared responsibility.
god_plan_lines: Rome now becomes an explicit destination in the narrative. In [Acts 23:11](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/23.htm), the Lord will tell Paul that he must testify there as he has in Jerusalem. The later promise connects this intention with God’s continuing purpose, even though the route will include arrest and hardship.

[Romans 15:25–27](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/15.htm) also shows Gentile churches sharing material help with believers in Jerusalem. The expanding mission does not discard earlier communities: people who have received spiritual blessings express their unity through practical care.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
